headline: Oil sinks on US-Iran peace hopes while AI spending doubts drag the Nasdaq lower
subhead: WTI fell 7.5 percent to 96.35 dollars and gold rose 1.9 percent, but the Nasdaq lost 1.1 percent and the S&P 500 0.5 percent to 7,541 as Intel and Oracle each dropped 8.8 percent.

us.text: The S&P 500 fell 0.5 percent to 7,541 and the Nasdaq 1.1 percent; the Dow rose 0.4 percent as most non-tech stocks gained on cheaper oil.
Intel and Oracle each fell 8.8 percent and Microsoft 2.8 percent as doubts over AI spending returns pushed the Nasdaq 100 into correction.
Apple beat estimates with 114.5 billion dollars of revenue but weaker guidance sent shares lower after hours; midterms vote today, payrolls Friday.

india.text: Nifty rose 388 points to 23,441 and Sensex 1,233 points on Monday as Reliance surged on results; price cards still show Friday's data.
Foreign investors net bought 3,115 crore rupees in cash on Monday while domestic institutions net sold 392 crore (provisional).
The rupee slipped 10 paise to 94.86 per dollar on a firm greenback despite lower crude; SBI reports second quarter results today.

global.text: Asia was mixed Monday: Kospi closed at 5,859 on chip exports, Nikkei near 63,082; Seoul fell 0.9 percent Tuesday with Samsung down 4.5 percent.
Europe closed higher as oil fell, with the DAX at 25,981 and FTSE 100 at 10,761, while BP fell 5.0 percent and Shell 3.5 percent in New York.
WTI fell 7.5 percent after Iran signalled openness to peace talks, lifting gold 1.9 percent and silver 3.6 percent as Fed hike fears eased.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on whether AI spending pays: Alphabet had its worst day on record after negative free cash flow, ServiceNow and Caterpillar sank on guidance, and Intel and Amazon closed the week with a broad tech sell-off that left the Nasdaq down 2.0 percent and the S&P 500 down 0.6 percent. The Fed held rates on 28 October with two officials favouring a hike, and with oil lifted by fresh Hormuz attacks, rate fears hit metals hardest: gold lost 2.7 percent on the week to near a 52 week low and silver 8.6 percent. India moved the other way, with the Nifty back above 23,000 on IT and pharma buying, Trent jumping on results and foreign investors turning net buyers on Friday. Crypto absorbed a 6.3 billion dollar Binance hack, leaving Bitcoin down 4.8 percent in the week to 30 October. Next week brings Apple results on 2 November, the US midterm elections on 3 November, the Bank of England on 5 November and US payrolls on 6 November.
